title: formatTruncatedToolOutput: negative maxChars silently inflates output ~2x

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue provides a clear, detailed, and actionable bug report describing a defect in formatTruncatedToolOutput where non-positive maxChars values cause output inflation instead of returning the content unchanged. It includes code snippets, root cause analysis, and reproducible unit test cases.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: This is a localized single-file logic bug in packages/core/src/utils/fileUtils.ts requiring a guard condition for maxChars <= 0 and unit tests in packages/core/src/utils/fileUtils.test.ts.

summary.problem: formatTruncatedToolOutput inflates output size or incorrectly wraps content in a truncation message when maxChars is non-positive.
summary.root_cause: formatTruncatedToolOutput lacks a check for maxChars <= 0. When maxChars is non-positive, the contentStr.length <= maxChars check fails for non-empty content, causing negative or zero slice indices that return and duplicate full content in the output.
summary.context: The function formatTruncatedToolOutput is part of the public exports of @google/gemini-cli-core. Non-positive maxChars values are conventionally used to disable truncation.

steps: In packages/core/src/utils/fileUtils.ts, modify formatTruncatedToolOutput to return contentStr early when maxChars <= 0.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: formatTruncatedToolOutput returns contentStr unchanged when maxChars is 0 or negative.
verification_steps: Add a unit test in packages/core/src/utils/fileUtils.test.ts verifying that formatTruncatedToolOutput returns contentStr unchanged when maxChars is 0.
Add a unit test in packages/core/src/utils/fileUtils.test.ts verifying that formatTruncatedToolOutput returns contentStr unchanged when maxChars is negative (e.g., -1000).
